en: n. the opinion that people in general have about someone or something; a good name that someone has earned
ex: The restaurant has a good reputation for fresh seafood.
這家餐廳以新鮮海鮮享有好名聲。

en: n. the process of coming to live permanently in a foreign country; the place at an airport or border where people's documents are checked
ex: Immigration to the country has increased sharply in recent years.
近年來移入該國的移民大幅增加。

en: n. a person whose job is to repair or maintain machines, especially car engines; a. relating to machines or manual work
ex: The mechanic fixed my car in less than an hour.
技師不到一小時就修好了我的車。

en: a. extremely angry; very strong or violent; wild and noisy
ex: She was furious when she found out the truth.
她發現真相時氣瘋了。

en: n. a person who fights against the government or refuses to obey rules; vi. to fight against authority or refuse to obey; a. fighting against the government or refusing to obey
ex: The teenager rebelled against his parents' strict rules.
那名青少年反抗父母的嚴格規定。

en: n. a person or organization that is trying to win something or to be more successful than others
ex: Our main competitor has just lowered its prices.
我們的主要競爭對手剛降價了。

en: a. unusual and surprising in a way that makes people notice or admire it; worthy of attention
ex: She has made remarkable progress in her English this year.
她今年的英文進步驚人。

en: n. the group of elected politicians who make laws in some countries, especially the United States; a formal meeting of representatives
ex: Congress voted to approve the new budget.
國會投票通過了新預算。

en: n. a scientist who studies physics, the science of matter, energy, motion and force
ex: The physicist won the Nobel Prize for his work on light.
那位物理學家因對光的研究獲得諾貝爾獎。

en: n. a room used for a particular purpose, especially a formal one; a group of people who make laws; a space inside something, such as a heart or gun; vt. to put a bullet in a gun
ex: The council chamber was filled with angry citizens.
議事廳裡擠滿了憤怒的市民。

en: n. the practice of training people to obey rules; the ability to control your own behavior; a particular area of study; vt. to train someone to obey rules; to punish someone
ex: Good discipline is important in a classroom.
良好的紀律在教室裡很重要。

en: a. real and not false or copied; sincere and honest; truly what it is said to be
ex: Is this a genuine leather bag or an imitation?
這是真皮包還是仿冒品？

en: a. producing a lot of goods or results; achieving a lot; making good use of time or effort
ex: We had a productive meeting and solved several problems.
我們開了一場有成效的會議，解決了好幾個問題。

en: n. a word or phrase used to express anger; a spell that is supposed to bring bad luck; something that causes great harm; vt. to use rude words to express anger; to wish bad luck on someone
ex: The witch put a curse on the village.
女巫對村莊下了詛咒。

en: n. a fact or event that makes a situation the way it is; the conditions that affect a situation; the way you live, especially how much money you have
ex: Under no circumstances should you open this door.
在任何情況下你都不該開這扇門。

en: n. an official list of names or items; a machine that records and stores money; the range of a voice or musical instrument; vt. to put your name on an official list; to show or express a feeling; to send a letter by registered mail; vi. to put your name on an official list
ex: You must register before you can use the library.
你必須先註冊才能使用圖書館。

en: a. most important or main; of the best quality; n. the best or most active part of something; the period of greatest success; vt. to prepare something for use; to give someone information beforehand
ex: The prime minister held a press conference yesterday.
首相昨天舉行了記者會。

en: a. having the power to attract iron or steel; having a strong power to attract people; relating to magnets or magnetism
ex: She has a magnetic personality that draws people to her.
她有吸引人的個性，大家都被她吸引。

en: n. a flower, especially one that is highly valued or ornamental; the period when something is at its best; vi. to produce flowers; to be at one's most healthy or beautiful; vt. to make something flourish
ex: The roses are in full bloom in the garden.
花園裡的玫瑰正盛開著。

en: a. complete and total; not limited by anything; (of a ruler) having total power; n. something that is completely perfect or independent
ex: I have absolute confidence in my team.
我對我的團隊有絕對的信心。

en: vt. to show how something works or how to do something; to prove that something is true; to show a feeling or quality; vi. to take part in a public protest
ex: The teacher demonstrated how to use the microscope.
老師示範如何使用顯微鏡。

en: n. a very strong feeling of fear; violent acts used to frighten people for political reasons; a person or thing that makes people frightened
ex: The children screamed in terror when they saw the snake.
孩子們看到蛇時嚇得尖叫。

en: vt. to press something so hard that it is broken or damaged; to defeat someone completely; to crowd people together; n. a crowd of people packed together; a strong feeling of love for someone, usually short-lived
ex: He accidentally crushed the box under his heavy bag.
他不小心用沉重的包包壓扁了盒子。

en: n. a crime or illegal act; an action that offends or upsets someone; an attack; the team in a game that is attempting to score
ex: I meant no offense by what I said.
我說的話沒有冒犯的意思。

en: a. willing to help or work with others; done by people working together; relating to a business owned by its workers or members
ex: The students were very cooperative during the experiment.
學生們在實驗期間非常合作。

en: n. the words and sentences that come before and after a word or phrase and help to explain its meaning; the situation in which something happens and that helps to explain it
ex: You need to read the whole paragraph to understand the context.
你得讀完整段才能理解上下文。

en: vt. to fasten or fix one thing to another; to connect yourself to a group or person; to give importance to something; vi. to belong to or be connected with something
ex: Please attach your résumé to the email.
請把你的履歷附加到電子郵件上。

en: n. a rough calculation of the size, amount or cost of something; an opinion about the value or quality of someone or something; vt. to guess or calculate something approximately; vi. to make a rough calculation
ex: The builder gave us an estimate of ten thousand dollars.
建商給了我們一萬元的估價。

en: a. allowed by the law; obeying the law; recognized by law as valid
ex: It is lawful to drive a car here only if you have a license.
只有持有駕照才能在這裡合法開車。

en: n. stories about imaginary people and events; something that is not true; a made-up story
ex: I enjoy reading science fiction in my free time.
我空閒時喜歡看科幻小說。

en: n. the state of being liked or admired by many people; the fact of being widely used or accepted; the state of being popular
ex: The singer's popularity has grown rapidly this year.
那位歌手的人氣今年迅速攀升。

en: v. to find a number or amount by using mathematics; to guess or predict something; to plan something carefully
ex: Can you calculate how much we need to pay for the trip?
你能算出我們這趟旅行要付多少錢嗎？

en: n. a fact or event in nature or society that can be observed, especially one that is unusual or interesting; a remarkable person or thing
ex: Rainbows are a natural phenomenon caused by sunlight and water.
彩虹是由陽光與水造成的自然現象。

en: adv. used to add another fact or idea to what has already been said
ex: The plan is simple; furthermore, it is cheap.
這個計畫很簡單；而且，它很便宜。

en: n. a society or culture that has developed a high level of social organization and technology; the process by which a society becomes more developed
ex: Ancient Egypt was one of the earliest great civilizations.
古埃及是最早的偉大文明之一。

en: n. a person who goes to live in a new country or area, usually in a way that changes the area; a person or thing that settles a matter or argument
ex: The early settlers built log cabins near the river.
早期的移民者在河邊蓋了木屋。

en: n. an illness caused by bacteria or a virus; the process of passing a disease to another person; a spreading of an idea or feeling
ex: The doctor gave her antibiotics for the ear infection.
醫生開了抗生素給她治療耳朵感染。

en: n. a person, especially a police officer, whose job is to find out who committed a crime; a person employed to investigate crimes; a. relating to the work of finding out about crimes
ex: The detective examined the room for clues.
偵探在房間裡搜尋線索。

en: n. the scientific study of living things and the way they behave and grow
ex: She is studying biology because she wants to become a doctor.
她研讀生物學，因為她想當醫生。

en: n. a large group of animals of one kind that live and feed together; a large group of people; a person who looks after a group of animals; vt. to make animals move together as a group; vi. to gather in a crowd
ex: A herd of cattle was grazing in the field.
一群牛正在田裡吃草。
